title: Ship Production Software in Minutes, Not Months — Eno Reyes, Factory
talk_summary: Factory's Eno Reyes argues agent-native development requires centralized context, standardized documentation as a knowledge base for agents, and agents used across planning, coding, and incident response—not just code generation. The talk is mostly vision and product pitch, but contains a few concrete mechanisms around context capture, planning decomposition, and incident/RCA automation.

takeaways.technique: Capture all meetings/transcripts into agent-accessible memory
takeaways.what_they_do: They transcribe every interaction and meeting, combine with architecture docs and ad hoc notes, and feed it to a 'knowledge droid' to find patterns and constraints before planning.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We transcribe every single interaction and meeting at factory.

takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of asking 'plan the feature', they ask targeted questions (find patterns in feedback, highlight technical constraints), produce 4-5 intermediate docs, then iterate a PRD that becomes a dependency-mapped ticket set for parallel agents.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We don't say, 'Let's plan the feature out.' We say, 'Could you find any patterns in the customer feedback...'
takeaways.numbers: eight tickets parallelized among eight code droids

takeaways.technique: Standardized docs as agent knowledge base (PRD/RCA/runbook templates)
takeaways.what_they_do: They treat PRDs, design docs, RCA templates, and roadmaps as a knowledge base agents learn and imitate, explicitly encoding the 'why' behind decisions.
takeaways.evidence_quote: your process and your documentation is a knowledge base and a map for your droids to learn and imitate

takeaways.technique: Agent-generated RCA and mitigation from incident alerts
takeaways.what_they_do: On alert, a droid pulls logs, past incidents, runbooks, and Slack discussion to produce an RCA and mitigation plan, then generates/updates runbooks from learned patterns.
takeaways.evidence_quote: a droid take a sentry incident and convert it into a full RCA and mitigation plan
takeaways.numbers: cut incident response time in half (claimed)

takeaways.technique: Agents question the task before executing
takeaways.what_they_do: The droid grounds itself, then returns a plan and asks clarifying questions rather than taking instructions at face value.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We need to expect our agents to not just take what we say at face value, but instead question it

takeaways.technique: Pre-commit hooks and lint gates inside agent loop
takeaways.what_they_do: The droid runs pre-commit hooks and lints itself before generating a PR that passes CI.
takeaways.evidence_quote: runs pre-commit hooks, lints, and ultimately generates a pull request that passes CI
